tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

files.description: File paths (absolute or relative to cwd) to send to the user. Always pass an array, even for a single file.

caption.description: Optional short caption for the file(s).

status.description: Use 'proactive' when you're surfacing a file the user hasn't asked for and needs to see now — a generated artifact, a completed report. Use 'normal' when replying to something the user just said.

display.description: How the client should present the file. 'render' opens it inline in the side panel (for HTML, SVG, Mermaid, images, PDFs — anything the user wants to look at now). 'attach' shows a download card only, no inline preview (for deliverables the user will save and open elsewhere). Omit to let the client decide by file type — today that means renderable types render and everything else attaches, same as before this parameter existed.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. # BMW Challenge: AI for Product Decision Making

An AI-powered application that helps BMW product managers (PMs) derive, justify and prioritize customer requirements for a **successor vehicle**, with the PM in control of every decision. This folder is the knowledge base: the challenge, the provided data (raw and processed), what BMW people told us, and our own notes.

> **Agents:** start with [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md). It has the reading order, ground rules and where each kind of fact lives.

## Quick facts
- **Task:** concept + working prototype that turns heterogeneous inputs into prioritized, evidence-backed, customer-facing requirements, with human review and a full audit trail.
- **Vehicles:** 1 Series (F70), 5 Series (G60, China G68), 7 Series (G70). **Markets:** Europe, China, US (any subset). **Horizon:** 3 to 5 years.
- **Must deliver:** (1) prototype, (2) sample requirement list with ID, description, findings and sources, score, rationale, evidence level, assumptions and status, (3) end-to-end workflow with AI and human boundaries, (4) audit trail.
- **Judged on:** scoring logic, workflow and human decisions, traceability, usability and feasibility, innovation and scalability. **Honesty about uncertainty is rewarded.**
- **Out of scope:** regulation and homologation, engineering specs, pricing and business case (cost only as a rough factor).
- **Biggest data caveat:** no customer feedback from China; G60/G70 feedback is 90 to 95% US; F70 is UK/Japan and ICE only.

## Map

```
BMW-Challenge/
├── CLAUDE.md                 Agent entry point: reading order, rules, where to find what
├── GLOSSARY.md               Model codes, BMW/process terms, German option-list terms
├── 01-challenge/             What we are asked to build, and what BMW wants
├── 02-data/                  Provided BMW data: raw/, processed/ (CSV), insights, equipment
├── 03-meetings/              Meeting summaries (raw/ holds the transcripts)
├── 04-team-notes/            Our own brainstorming
└── 05-solution/              Our solution design: scope/focus, end-to-end flow, UX decisions
```

### 01-challenge: the task
| File | Content |
|---|---|
| [`hackathon-briefing.md`](01-challenge/hackathon-briefing.md) / [`.pdf`](01-challenge/hackathon-briefing.pdf) | Official brief: challenge, mission, what to demonstrate (the .md matches the 2-page PDF) |
| [`mission-and-deliverables.md`](01-challenge/mission-and-deliverables.md) | Mission sheet: scope, in/out of scope, the 4 deliverables, audit trail |
| [`evaluation-criteria.md`](01-challenge/evaluation-criteria.md) | **The 5 judging criteria** + "we reward honesty" + what to show for each |
| [`stakeholder-needs.md`](01-challenge/stakeholder-needs.md) | **Consolidated needs** from all documents and interviews, with source tags: functional needs, principles, prioritization signals, open questions |
| [`process-cycle.md`](01-challenge/process-cycle.md) | BMW's process slide: situation analysis → structure → definition → prioritization → documentation |
| [`findings-to-requirements.md`](01-challenge/findings-to-requirements.md) | 1 billion findings → 1,000 requirements → one car (example verbatims and requirements) |
| [`smart-requirements.md`](01-challenge/smart-requirements.md) | How to write a requirement (SMART), good and bad examples, the requirement record template |
| [`product-development-process.md`](01-challenge/product-development-process.md) | Generic 13-phase automotive process with gates, and where our tool sits (phases 1 and 2) |
| [`provided-data-overview.md`](01-challenge/provided-data-overview.md) | What each provided dataset is good for |
| `assets/` | Source slide images |

# BMW Challenge: AI for Product Decision Making

An AI-powered application that helps BMW product managers derive, justify and prioritize customer requirements for a successor vehicle, with the product manager in control of every decision. This folder holds the challenge material, provided data, meeting notes and team ideas.

## Structure

```
All-context/
├── GLOSSARY.md                Model codes, BMW and process terms, German option-list terms
├── 01-challenge/              What we are asked to build, and what BMW wants
├── 02-data-provided-by-pm/    Provided BMW data: raw/, processed/ (CSV and text), insights, equipment baseline
├── 03-meetings-with-pm/       Meeting summaries and notes (raw/ holds the transcripts)
├── 04-team-notes/             Our early brainstorm, open questions, notes between teammates
├── 05-web-sources/            External sources for the fetch agents
└── 06-solution-concept/       Solution concept from the UI side: scope, end-to-end flow, UX decisions
```

This is the single knowledge base: the former `docs/` folder of the frontend branch was merged into it on 2026-10-11 (identical files dropped, new files moved here). The fixed classification lives in [`../taxonomy/`](../taxonomy/README.md).

{
  "name": "web",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "private": true,
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "next dev",
    "build": "next build",
    "start": "next start",
    "lint": "eslint",
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit",
    "seed": "tsx scripts/seed.ts",
    "export-contract": "tsx scripts/export-contract.ts",
    "contract-test": "tsx scripts/contract-test.ts",
    "map-test": "tsx scripts/map-test.ts",
    "adapter-flow": "tsx scripts/adapter-flow.ts"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "@anthropic-ai/sdk": "^0.133.0",
    "@dnd-kit/core": "^6.3.1",
    "@dnd-kit/sortable": "^10.0.0",
    "@dnd-kit/utilities": "^3.2.2",
    "@tanstack/react-query": "^5.104.1",
    "class-variance-authority": "^0.7.1",
    "cmdk": "^1.1.1",
    "cn": "^0.4.0",
    "diff": "^9.0.0",
    "lucide-react": "^1.55.0",
    "next": "16.4.0",
    "next-themes": "^0.4.6",
    "pptxgenjs": "^4.0.1",
# Argon (web)

The clickable demo of our BMW hackathon tool: **Signals → Cases → Requirements → Vehicle plan**. It runs on synthetic data behind a real REST contract, so the team can work in three tracks at once and replace the mock backend later with no UI changes.

- **Signal:** one piece of evidence with its source. Either a real BMW record (verbatim, study row) or a web finding (synthetic in the demo).
- **Case:** a customer problem built from signals. It has an importance score but no cost. The PM works it with open questions, meeting notes and Argus, the AI assistant, then decides one of: confirm, refer, innovation pool, park, merge or reject.
- **Requirement:** what BMW builds, created from a confirmed case. It carries a SMART text, measurable targets, a release (next generation, mid-life update or OTA) and a rough cost. It moves from draft through discussion and PM approval to head sign-off, then the vehicle plan, then Codebeamer export.

## Screens (six, after Thomas's "less is more" feedback)

| Nav | What the PM does there |
|---|---|
| **My desk** | Four cards sorted by kind of work: *Agent flags* (competitor alerts, @mentions) · *My cases* · *Review* (requirements sent back or in progress; for the head: regional brief differences, sign-off and escalations inline) · *Follow up* (answers that came back, questions due) |
| **Inbox** | Referrals to accept or decline, agent flags, all notifications |
| **Cases** | Kanban (drag = state change with a reason). A *Ranked* toggle shows the score order; weights sit behind one button |
| **Vehicle plan** | All requirements of a series as a list grouped by car area, with status filter chips, plan action and release; today's equipment folds per area; Codebeamer export |
| **Signals** | One Sankey: sources → car areas → cases. Click a node to see its signals and start a case from loose ones. *Refresh* plays the agent run step by step (fetch → classify → gate → match metrics → assess impact) |
| **Innovation pool** | Ideas parked for a future series; vote or pull into your series |

Three things borrowed from the market (see the competitor research):
- **Quality check on every requirement** (like Raiqon and Polarion run inside Codebeamer): vague wording, scope vs. evidence, out-of-scope content (regulatory, technical, pricing), duplicates, conflicting targets and Baukasten overlap. Rules always run; with an LLM key an AI pass adds issues. It warns but never blocks: *Approve as PM* lists the open issues and the reason is logged.
- **Ask the segment** in the case chat (like Dovetail's digital twins, but grounded): chips such as *USA (24) · USA BEV (9) · China (0)* answer only from that segment's real BMW verbatims, with citations. No verbatims means "no evidence" plus a proposed open question, never a guess.
- **Engineering deck** next to *Export to Codebeamer* (like Aha! roadmap decks): one slide per signed-off or planned requirement with the SMART text, three customer quotes, the score breakdown, the competition and the decision log.

A **case** opens with a Sankey of its evidence (*sources → what they say → case*, where "what they say" is a taxonomy topic × type, e.g. *Public charging · hard to use*). Every node is clickable and shows its quotes. Then three steps: **① Evidence** (Sankey + three bullets, full analysis on demand) → **② Your stance** (brief values you inherit, overridable with a reason; your take on the evidence; what you know that the data can't show; how far to go. import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";

/**
 * The brand marks (docs/design/logos). Argon: the full outer shell of eight
 * electrons (argon is inert, it never reacts on its own) around a navy core.
 * Argus, the AI: an eye with argon's violet glow as the iris and a navy spark.
 * Lines take the text colour, so both work in light and dark mode.
 */
const navy = "var(--mark-navy, var(--brand-navy, #1e3a8a))";

const SHELL = [0, 45, 90, 135, 180, 225, 270, 315].map((deg) => [32 + 22 * Math.sin((deg * Math.PI) / 180), 32 - 22 * Math.cos((deg * Math.PI) / 180)]);

export function ArgonMark({ className }: { className?: string }) {
  return (
    <svg viewBox="0 0 64 64" aria-hidden className={cn("size-6 shrink-0", className)}>
      <circle cx="32" cy="32" r="22" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth="1.5" opacity=".25" />
      {SHELL.map(([x, y]) => (
        <circle key={`${x}-${y}`} cx={x} cy={y} r="3.6" fill="currentColor" />
      ))}
      <circle cx="32" cy="32" r="9" fill={navy} />
    </svg>
  );
}

export function ArgusMark({ className }: { className?: string }) {
  return (
    <svg viewBox="0 0 64 64" aria-hidden className={cn("size-4 shrink-0", className)}>
      {/* Eye white, then the outline: a soft fill so the eye reads as a shape on any surface. */}
      <path d="M3 34C13 15 51 15 61 34C51 53 13 53 3 34Z" fill="currentColor" fillOpacity=".14" />
      <path d="M3 34C13 15 51 15 61 34C51 53 13 53 3 34Z" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth="5" strokeLinejoin="round" />
      {/* Iris with a darker rim, a large pupil and two highlights. */}
      <circle cx="32" cy="34" r="13" fill="var(--brand-violet, #7c5cff)" />
      <circle cx="32" cy="34" r="13" fill="none" stroke="#09090b" strokeOpacity=".35" strokeWidth="2" />
      <circle cx="32" cy="34" r="5.6" fill="#09090b" />
      <circle cx="36.4" cy="29.6" r="2.6" fill="#fff" />
      <circle cx="27.8" cy="38.2" r="1.1" fill="#fff" fillOpacity=".8" />
      <path d="M54 1C55 6.4 57.1 8.5 62.5 9.5C57.1 10.5 55 12.6 54 18C53 12.6 50.9 10.5 45.5 9.5C50.9 8.5 53 6.4 54 1Z" fill={navy} />
    </svg>
  );
}

lines: -name: ux-audit-cases
-description: Read-only UX auditor for the Cases board and the case page (3 steps, Sankey, case stance).
-readonly: true
-# ux-audit-cases

-You are a **read-only auditor**. Do not edit, create or delete any file and do not run any command that changes the repo, the app or the demo store (no Reset demo data, no clicks that save, decide, refresh or post). Do not run the gate script against port 3000. Observe and report only; your final message is your report.
-## Your area: Cases board and case page
-Persona: Lena (`u-lena`).
-Question: **is it obvious where you are in the case and what the next step is?**

-Evidence: baseline screens `cases-board_*`, `case-evidence_*`, `case-stance_*`, `case-requirements_*`. Code: `web/src/app/(app)/cases/cases-view.tsx`, `web/src/app/(app)/cases/[id]/case-view.tsx`, `web/src/components/cases/*` (stance-form, shape-form, case-action-dialog, weight panel), `web/src/components/sankey/sankey-chart.tsx`, `web/src/lib/sankey.ts`.

-Check: the step indicator and the "Next" buttons, the alert banner, the many header buttons (Watch, Details, Comments, More, AI colleague, Decide), the evidence bullets vs. "Read full analysis", the stance form density, open questions, the honesty signals (evidence level, market coverage) that must stay visible.
-# UX intuitiveness pass: shared brief (goal, boundary, rubrics, app, output format)
-Every audit, fix and verification agent works from this brief. It is copied verbatim into each agent file in `.cursor/agents/`.
-## The goal

-The product must be **as easy to understand as Jira**: not the same features, the same level of "I get it at a glance". It should feel clean and calm, not overwhelming, while still giving enough context to be helpful. A product manager who has never seen it should know on each screen: **where am I, what needs my attention, what is the one next thing to do.**

-Background you can read (read-only): `web/README.md` (screens, personas, demo scripts), `All-context/06-solution-concept/ux-and-collaboration.md`, `All-context/03-meetings-with-pm/2026-10-10_2308_thomas-demo-feedback_summary.md` (BMW's feedback: "less is more", a PM must understand it "in one look").
-## THE BOUNDARY (read this twice)
-This pass changes **small details with a big UX impact**. It does **not** change the product.
-**Allowed (micro-level presentation):**

-- **Progressive disclosure:** a long analysis that is always shown becomes a one-line summary that expands into the full analysis on click. Secondary panels are collapsed by default. "Show more" on long lists.
-- **Visual hierarchy:** one clear primary button per screen or section; others become secondary/ghost. Mute metadata. Fix spacing, alignment and type scale. Reduce badge and colour noise.
-- **Microcopy:** button labels as verbs ("Confirm case", not "OK"), shorter headings, jargon explained with a tooltip or inline hint, consistent terms for the same thing across screens.
-- **States:** empty states that say what goes here and offer the one next action; loading skeletons; clear success/error toasts; disabled buttons say why they are disabled.
-- **Wayfinding:** breadcrumbs or back links, page titles that match the nav label, visible current location, sensible default sort and filter, counts on tabs.
-- **Accessibility:** focus states, keyboard reachability, contrast, labels, alt text, hit-target sizes.
-- Reusing existing shadcn components (Collapsible, Accordion, Tooltip, Skeleton, empty-state patterns) instead of custom ones.
-**Forbidden (if a finding needs one of these, report it under "Needs a product decision" and do NOT implement it):**
-- Adding, removing, merging or reordering screens, nav items, workflow steps, case/requirement states, outcomes or gates.
-- Changing roles, permissions, the data model, `web/src/contracts`, the mock backend logic (`web/src/mock`), the seed data or the AI behaviour.
-- Removing any information or feature. Hiding it behind a disclosure is fine, as long as it stays **reachable in one click** and the summary line tells you what's inside.

-- Hiding or weakening **honesty signals**: data-coverage warnings ("no China verbatims", "90% US"), evidence level, assumption vs. evidence labels, "no evidence" answers, quality-check issues, the AI-vs-human marking. These may be made more compact but must stay **visible without a click**. They are what the jury rewards.
-- Changing the demo storyline in `web/README.md` (the steps must still work exactly as written).
-- Visual redesign: new colour palette, new fonts, new layout system, restyled brand. Polish, don't redesign.
-When unsure: it's forbidden. Ask.
-## Rubrics

-- NN/g's 10 usability heuristics: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/ (cite by number 1–10: 1 visibility of system status, 2 match with the real world, 3 user control and freedom, 4 consistency and standards, 5 error prevention, 6 recognition rather than recall, 7 flexibility and efficiency, 8 aesthetic and minimalist design, 9 help users recognize/diagnose/recover from errors, 10 help and documentation).

-- Cognitive walkthrough, 4 questions per step: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/cognitive-walkthroughs/ (Will the user try to achieve the right result? Will they notice the correct action is available? Will they associate the action with the result? Will they see progress after the action?)
-- Progressive disclosure: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/progressive-disclosure/
-- Severity on Nielsen's 0–4 scale: 0 not a problem, 1 cosmetic, 2 minor, 3 major, 4 usability catastrophe.

-- Code rules: the Vercel Web Interface Guidelines in `.cursor/skills/web-design-guidelines/guidelines.md` (offline copy; source https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines/main/command.md).
-## The app

-- `web/` is Next.js 16, React 19, Tailwind 4, shadcn/ui (`web/src/components/ui`), a mock backend at `/api` (`web/src/mock`, do not change). Screens live in `web/src/app/(app)/*`, building blocks in `web/src/components/*`.

-- Nav (six items): My desk `/`, Inbox `/inbox`, Cases `/cases` (case page `/cases/<id>` with three steps: ① Evidence, ② Your stance `?step=knowledge`, ③ Requirements `?step=requirements`), Vehicle plan `/plan/G60`, Signals `/radar`, Innovation pool `/innovation`. Not in the nav: Settings `/settings`, Audit `/audit`, series brief `/brief` (persona menu), requirement page `/requirements/<id>`, ripple `/ripple/<id>`, Replay (overlay from the *Replay* button on a requirement).

-- Personas (cookie `rs_user`): `u-lena` (PM 5 Series RoW), `u-wei` (PM 5 Series China, not onboarded on a fresh store), `u-jonas` (HMI cross-series), `u-katrin` (head of product line), `u-sofia` (1 Series), `u-daniel` (7 Series).

-- **Baseline evidence (the "before")**: `docs/ux-audit/baseline/index.md` and `docs/ux-audit/baseline/screens/<state>_<1440|768>_<light|dark>.png`, plus axe and Lighthouse results in `docs/ux-audit/baseline/results.json`. Read the PNGs with the Read tool.

## Run it

```bash
npm install
```

```bash
npm run dev
```

Open http://localhost:3000 and pick a persona. The persona menu (top right) switches users and has **Reset demo data**.

| Script | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` / `build` / `start` | Next.js 16 app plus the mock backend at `/api` |
| `npm run seed` | Rebuilds `src/mock/fixtures/seed.json` from the real CSVs in `All-context/02-data-provided-by-pm/processed/` plus the authored content. Validated against the contract |
| `npm run export-contract` | Writes `../contracts/openapi.yaml` and `../contracts/schemas/*.json` |
| `npm run contract-test` | Calls every endpoint against a running backend (`API_BASE`, default `http://localhost:3000/api`) and validates each response. Also walks the demo storyline |
| `npm run typecheck` / `lint` | Static checks |

Optional live AI chat: set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (optionally `LLM_MODEL`). Free-form chat questions then go to Claude with the case as context. Proposals, drafts and research stay scripted so they keep the contract. Without a key the scripted assistant answers offline. The team docs name OpenAI as the provider; to switch, change the single function in `src/mock/ai/live.ts`.

## How the code is split (three tracks)

```
contracts/                 (repo root) generated OpenAPI + JSON Schemas for the backend team
web/src/contracts/         Zod schemas = THE contract (enums, entities, endpoints, UI labels)
web/src/lib/api/           typed client (base URL: NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL, default /api) + TanStack Query hooks
web/src/app/(app)/         screens                                   ← frontend track
web/src/components/        UI building blocks (shadcn/ui in components/ui)
web/src/app/api/[...path]  MOCK BACKEND: one route implementing every endpoint   ← replaced by the backend track
web/src/mock/              in-memory store, reference scoring, scripted AI, seed fixtures   ← logic + data track
web/scripts/               seed, contract export, contract test
```

| Track | Owns | Works against |
|---|---|---|
| **Frontend** | `src/app/(app)`, `src/components` | `src/lib/api` hooks only (never imports `src/mock`) |
| **Backend / API** | A FastAPI service on Supabase (Ghassen's `data-model.mmd`) implementing `contracts/openapi.yaml` | `npm run contract-test` with `API_BASE=<their url>`; then set `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` |
| **Logic + data** | Fetch agents, clustering, scoring, requirement drafting, chat/RAG, meeting-note extraction | The reference behaviour in `src/mock/scoring.ts`, `src/mock/ai/*` and the seed. Same inputs and outputs |

**Changing the contract:** edit `src/contracts/*.ts`, then run `npm run typecheck`, which shows every UI and mock spot to update. Then run `npm run export-contract` and commit `contracts/` so the backend sees the change.

**Rules the contract encodes (keep them in the real backend):**
- The acting user comes in as header `x-user-id` (mock auth); the real backend uses a token.
- Every status change needs a `rationale` and writes an `AuditEvent` (actor = person or `agent:<name>`).
- The AI never edits directly: it returns `Proposal`s (field, body, question answer, new question, new requirement) that a PM accepts or rejects.
- Only the owner or a co-owner changes a case or requirement. The head of product line signs off and resolves escalations. Everyone can read, comment, watch and escalate.
- Case score = weighted mean of 8 factors (0..1), with no cost. Requirement rank = case score × cost multiplier (S/M/L). Evidence level is separate from the score.

### Contract additions vs. `data-model.mmd` (to sync with Ghassen)

Open http://localhost:3000 and pick a persona. The persona menu (top right) switches users and has **Reset demo data**.

| Script | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` / `build` / `start` | Next.js 16 app plus the mock backend at `/api` |
| `npm run seed` | Rebuilds `src/mock/fixtures/seed.json` from the real CSVs in `All-context/02-data-provided-by-pm/processed/` plus the authored content. Validated against the contract |
| `npm run export-contract` | Writes `../contracts/openapi.yaml` and `../contracts/schemas/*.json` |
| `npm run contract-test` | Calls every endpoint against a running backend (`API_BASE`, default `http://localhost:3000/api`) and validates each response. Also walks the demo storyline |
| `npm run typecheck` / `lint` | Static checks |

Optional live AI chat: set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (optionally `LLM_MODEL`). Free-form chat questions then go to Claude with the case as context. Proposals, drafts and research stay scripted so they keep the contract. Without a key the scripted assistant answers offline. The team docs name OpenAI as the provider; to switch, change the single function in `src/mock/ai/live.ts`.

## How the code is split (three tracks)

```
contracts/                 (repo root) generated OpenAPI + JSON Schemas for the backend team
web/src/contracts/         Zod schemas = THE contract (enums, entities, endpoints, UI labels)
web/src/lib/api/           typed client (base URL: NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL, default /api) + TanStack Query hooks
web/src/app/(app)/         screens                                   ← frontend track
web/src/components/        UI building blocks (shadcn/ui in components/ui)
web/src/app/api/[...path]  MOCK BACKEND: one route implementing every endpoint   ← replaced by the backend track
web/src/mock/              in-memory store, reference scoring, scripted AI, seed fixtures   ← logic + data track
web/scripts/               seed, contract export, contract test
```

| Track | Owns | Works against |
|---|---|---|
| **Frontend** | `src/app/(app)`, `src/components` | `src/lib/api` hooks only (never imports `src/mock`) |
| **Backend / API** | A FastAPI service on Supabase (Ghassen's `data-model.mmd`) implementing `contracts/openapi.yaml` | `npm run contract-test` with `API_BASE=<their url>`; then set `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` |
| **Logic + data** | Fetch agents, clustering, scoring, requirement drafting, chat/RAG, meeting-note extraction | The reference behaviour in `src/mock/scoring.ts`, `src/mock/ai/*` and the seed. Same inputs and outputs |

**Changing the contract:** edit `src/contracts/*.ts`, then run `npm run typecheck`, which shows every UI and mock spot to update. Then run `npm run export-contract` and commit `contracts/` so the backend sees the change.

**Rules the contract encodes (keep them in the real backend):**
- The acting user comes in as header `x-user-id` (mock auth); the real backend uses a token.
- Every status change needs a `rationale` and writes an `AuditEvent` (actor = person or `agent:<name>`).
- The AI never edits directly: it returns `Proposal`s (field, body, question answer, new question, new requirement) that a PM accepts or rejects.
- Only the owner or a co-owner changes a case or requirement. The head of product line signs off and resolves escalations. Everyone can read, comment, watch and escalate.
- Case score = weighted mean of 8 factors (0..1), with no cost. Requirement rank = case score × cost multiplier (S/M/L). Evidence level is separate from the score.

AI that turns customer voice, market data and competitor research into prioritized, evidence-backed requirements for the next BMW, with the product manager in control of every decision.

TUM.ai Hackathon Final · BMW Group challenge "AI for Product Decision Making"

--- ## The problem A BMW product manager defining the **successor** of a vehicle line (3 to 5 years ahead) has to read thousands of customer verbatims, customer studies, option lists, competitor news and trend reports, then argue for the roughly **top 10 requirements** that go to engineering. In interviews, BMW PMs told us research is the bottleneck, and that a tool is only useful if it is **no black box**: every proposal must show its source, market and evidence, and the PM decides. ## What Argon does ``` Signal ──► Case (problem) ──► PM confirms ──► Requirement (solution) ──► PM approves ──► engineering ``` | Step | What it is | Who acts | |---|---|---| | **Signal** | One statement about one feature from one source record (a BMW verbatim, a review sentence, a competitor fact, a trend), with the exact quote, market and source link. Invalid signals go to a visible quarantine. | AI extracts, a validation gate checks every quote against the stored record | | **Case** | A customer problem built from a group of signals, e.g. *"Front seat ventilation too weak"*. Keeps all opinions per market and powertrain, so market conflicts become visible. Scored, but has no cost. | AI clusters, figures and tags; **PM confirms or rejects** | | **Requirement** | What BMW will build, customer-facing and measurable: target vs. today's value and competitors, acceptance criteria, release (next generation, mid-life update, OTA), rough cost S/M/L. Every sentence carries its provenance: evidence, PM context or assumption. | AI drafts after confirmation; **PM approves**, head of product line signs off | Everything is written to an **append-only audit trail** (actor, timestamp, before/after, rationale), from the source record to the human decision. A *trace replay* plays a requirement's whole life in about 15 seconds and re-checks the chain: every quote found in its source, every record hash intact, no gaps, a rationale on every status change. ### Highlights - **Fixed taxonomy, no invented themes.** Every signal is classified into BMW's own labels: 219 topics, 11 aspect groups, 11 car areas ([`taxonomy/`](taxonomy/README.md)). - **Explainable, tunable score.** Case score = weighted factors (distinct customers, severity, satisfaction gap, competitor gap, market volume, removed vs. predecessor, capped reach, trend) × brand-fit multiplier. The PM switches weight profiles and sees which items stay on top regardless. Requirement rank = case score × cost multiplier. - **Reach is not relevance.** Distinct customers and capped reach keep one influencer from outranking a hundred owners. - **Markets are separate worlds.** Conflicts (one market negative, another positive) are flagged with statistics and never decided by the AI. - **Argus, the AI assistant.** A RAG sidebar on every case and requirement page that cites a signal ID for every claim ("no evidence found" otherwise) and proposes edits as diffs the PM accepts or rejects. - **Daily web loop.** Competitor, customer, trend and innovation agents fetch from a curated source list within a daily budget; page content is treated as data, and agents can only write signals, never cases. - **Collaboration built in.** Case ownership per line, series briefs, stances, open questions, referrals, an innovation pool, the vehicle plan and Codebeamer-style export. ## Run it **Demo UI (offline, synthetic data on top of real BMW verbatims):** ```bash cd web && npm install && npm run dev ``` Open http://localhost:3000, pick a persona, and use **Reset demo data** in the persona menu. Demo scripts are in [`web/README.md`](web/README.md). **Backend on a local embedded database (no Supabase, no OpenAI):** ```bash cd backend && uv run python -m app.dev_local ``` Then start the UI against it with `DATA_SOURCE=backend` (API on `http://localhost:8000`, OpenAPI at `/docs`). Tests run offline with `uv run pytest`. For the full Supabase + OpenAI setup, copy `backend/.env.example` to `backend/.env` and see [`backend/API.md`](backend/API.md) and [`HANDOFF.md`](HANDOFF.md). ## Architecture | Layer | Tech | |---|---| | UI | Next.js 16, React, Tailwind, shadcn/ui, TanStack Query; typed REST contract in Zod ([`web/src/contracts`](web/src/contracts), exported to [`contracts/`](contracts/openapi.yaml)) | | API and agents | Python 3.12, FastAPI, background fetch worker | | Storage | Supabase Postgres + pgvector (16 migrations), append-only audit table enforced in the database | | AI | OpenAI chat models for classification, extraction, case pages, tags, Argus and requirement texts; `text-embedding-3-small` (768 dims) for clustering and hybrid search. Every output stores its model and prompt version | Pipeline: configuration → one-time seed of BMW's data → daily fetch loop → signal validation gate → cases → case score → PM workspace → requirement generation → ranking and approval. The full diagram is [`architecture.mmd`](architecture.mmd). ## Data BMW provided customer feedback for the 1, 5 and 7 Series (about 10,000 verbatims), a 2025 customer study, sales volumes to 2030 and German option lists. They are kept unmodified in [`All-context/02-data-provided-by-pm/raw/`](All-context/02-data-provided-by-pm/README.md) and loaded from the original files, so every value keeps its sheet and row. Competitors and 3-to-5-year trends come only from web research and are labelled as external or assumption. Known gaps (no Chinese feedback, US-heavy 5 and 7 Series data, no dates, no study sample sizes) are shown in the product, not hidden. ## Repository | Path | Content | |---|---| | [`web/`](web/README.md) | The Argon UI and an offline mock backend that serves the same contract | | [`backend/`](backend/API.md) | API, agents, scoring, seed, Supabase migrations, tests and reports | | [`taxonomy/`](taxonomy/README.md) | The fixed classification (car areas, topics, aspect groups), build script and classifier eval | | [`contracts/`](contracts/openapi.yaml) | REST contract between UI and backend (OpenAPI 3.1 + JSON Schemas) | | [`All-context/`](All-context/README.md) | Challenge brief, provided data, PM interviews and meeting notes, web source list | | [`docs/`](docs/) | UI solution design, design assets and logos, UX audit reports | | [`landing/`](landing/index.html) | Intro loading page | | [`architecture.mmd`](architecture.mmd), [`database-design.md`](database-design.md), [`data-model.mmd`](data-model.mmd) | Pipeline, database design and ER diagram | | [`plan.md`](plan.md), [`changes.md`](changes.md), [`HANDOFF.md`](HANDOFF.md) | Implementation plan, every changed decision with its reason, current state | ## Team Built in one weekend at the TUM.ai hackathon by [Ghassen Zaara](https://github.com/ghassenzaara), [kechich](https://github.com/kechich), [Ahlem Trabelsi](https://github.com/ahlemtr) and [Amine Cheikhrouhou](https://github.com/AmineChr54). AI-assisted development sessions are recorded with [Entire](https://entire.io). A hackathon prototype, not an official BMW product. BMW data was provided for the challenge.

lines: -name: ux-audit-cases
-description: Read-only UX auditor for the Cases board and the case page (3 steps, Sankey, case stance).
-readonly: true
-# ux-audit-cases

-You are a **read-only auditor**. Do not edit, create or delete any file and do not run any command that changes the repo, the app or the demo store (no Reset demo data, no clicks that save, decide, refresh or post). Do not run the gate script against port 3000. Observe and report only; your final message is your report.
-## Your area: Cases board and case page
-Persona: Lena (`u-lena`).
-Question: **is it obvious where you are in the case and what the next step is?**

-Evidence: baseline screens `cases-board_*`, `case-evidence_*`, `case-stance_*`, `case-requirements_*`. Code: `web/src/app/(app)/cases/cases-view.tsx`, `web/src/app/(app)/cases/[id]/case-view.tsx`, `web/src/components/cases/*` (stance-form, shape-form, case-action-dialog, weight panel), `web/src/components/sankey/sankey-chart.tsx`, `web/src/lib/sankey.ts`.

-Check: the step indicator and the "Next" buttons, the alert banner, the many header buttons (Watch, Details, Comments, More, AI colleague, Decide), the evidence bullets vs. "Read full analysis", the stance form density, open questions, the honesty signals (evidence level, market coverage) that must stay visible.
-# UX intuitiveness pass: shared brief (goal, boundary, rubrics, app, output format)
-Every audit, fix and verification agent works from this brief. It is copied verbatim into each agent file in `.cursor/agents/`.
-## The goal

-The product must be **as easy to understand as Jira**: not the same features, the same level of "I get it at a glance". It should feel clean and calm, not overwhelming, while still giving enough context to be helpful. A product manager who has never seen it should know on each screen: **where am I, what needs my attention, what is the one next thing to do.**

-Background you can read (read-only): `web/README.md` (screens, personas, demo scripts), `docs/05-solution/ux-and-collaboration.md`, `docs/03-meetings/2026-10-10_2308_thomas-demo-feedback_summary.md` (BMW's feedback: "less is more", a PM must understand it "in one look").
-## THE BOUNDARY (read this twice)
-This pass changes **small details with a big UX impact**. It does **not** change the product.
-**Allowed (micro-level presentation):**

-- **Progressive disclosure:** a long analysis that is always shown becomes a one-line summary that expands into the full analysis on click. Secondary panels are collapsed by default. "Show more" on long lists.
-- **Visual hierarchy:** one clear primary button per screen or section; others become secondary/ghost. Mute metadata. Fix spacing, alignment and type scale. Reduce badge and colour noise.
-- **Microcopy:** button labels as verbs ("Confirm case", not "OK"), shorter headings, jargon explained with a tooltip or inline hint, consistent terms for the same thing across screens.
-- **States:** empty states that say what goes here and offer the one next action; loading skeletons; clear success/error toasts; disabled buttons say why they are disabled.
-- **Wayfinding:** breadcrumbs or back links, page titles that match the nav label, visible current location, sensible default sort and filter, counts on tabs.
-- **Accessibility:** focus states, keyboard reachability, contrast, labels, alt text, hit-target sizes.
-- Reusing existing shadcn components (Collapsible, Accordion, Tooltip, Skeleton, empty-state patterns) instead of custom ones.
-**Forbidden (if a finding needs one of these, report it under "Needs a product decision" and do NOT implement it):**
-- Adding, removing, merging or reordering screens, nav items, workflow steps, case/requirement states, outcomes or gates.
-- Changing roles, permissions, the data model, `web/src/contracts`, the mock backend logic (`web/src/mock`), the seed data or the AI behaviour.
-- Removing any information or feature. Hiding it behind a disclosure is fine, as long as it stays **reachable in one click** and the summary line tells you what's inside.

-- Hiding or weakening **honesty signals**: data-coverage warnings ("no China verbatims", "90% US"), evidence level, assumption vs. evidence labels, "no evidence" answers, quality-check issues, the AI-vs-human marking. These may be made more compact but must stay **visible without a click**. They are what the jury rewards.
-- Changing the demo storyline in `web/README.md` (the steps must still work exactly as written).
-- Visual redesign: new colour palette, new fonts, new layout system, restyled brand. Polish, don't redesign.
-When unsure: it's forbidden. Ask.
-## Rubrics

-- NN/g's 10 usability heuristics: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/ (cite by number 1–10: 1 visibility of system status, 2 match with the real world, 3 user control and freedom, 4 consistency and standards, 5 error prevention, 6 recognition rather than recall, 7 flexibility and efficiency, 8 aesthetic and minimalist design, 9 help users recognize/diagnose/recover from errors, 10 help and documentation).

-- Cognitive walkthrough, 4 questions per step: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/cognitive-walkthroughs/ (Will the user try to achieve the right result? Will they notice the correct action is available? Will they associate the action with the result? Will they see progress after the action?)
-- Progressive disclosure: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/progressive-disclosure/
-- Severity on Nielsen's 0–4 scale: 0 not a problem, 1 cosmetic, 2 minor, 3 major, 4 usability catastrophe.

-- Code rules: the Vercel Web Interface Guidelines in `.cursor/skills/web-design-guidelines/guidelines.md` (offline copy; source https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines/main/command.md).
-## The app

-- `web/` is Next.js 16, React 19, Tailwind 4, shadcn/ui (`web/src/components/ui`), a mock backend at `/api` (`web/src/mock`, do not change). Screens live in `web/src/app/(app)/*`, building blocks in `web/src/components/*`.

-- Nav (six items): My desk `/`, Inbox `/inbox`, Cases `/cases` (case page `/cases/<id>` with three steps: ① Evidence, ② Your stance `?step=knowledge`, ③ Requirements `?step=requirements`), Vehicle plan `/plan/G60`, Signals `/radar`, Innovation pool `/innovation`. Not in the nav: Settings `/settings`, Audit `/audit`, series brief `/brief` (persona menu), requirement page `/requirements/<id>`, ripple `/ripple/<id>`, Replay (overlay from the *Replay* button on a requirement).

-- Personas (cookie `rs_user`): `u-lena` (PM 5 Series RoW), `u-wei` (PM 5 Series China, not onboarded on a fresh store), `u-jonas` (HMI cross-series), `u-katrin` (head of product line), `u-sofia` (1 Series), `u-daniel` (7 Series).

-- **Baseline evidence (the "before")**: `docs/ux-audit/baseline/index.md` and `docs/ux-audit/baseline/screens/<state>_<1440|768>_<light|dark>.png`, plus axe and Lighthouse results in `docs/ux-audit/baseline/results.json`. Read the PNGs with the Read tool.

-- Extra headless screenshots of any state (no shared browser needed): `node .cursor/ux-gate/gate.mjs --out <dir> --only <names> --no-lighthouse` with targets from `.cursor/ux-gate/targets.json`. **Do not run it against port 3000 while other agents audit** (it resets the store); use `BASE_URL=http://localhost:3001` when a second server runs there.
-## Output format per finding
-One markdown table row each:

-`ID | screen/state | what's wrong (observed, not guessed) | heuristic # | severity 0–4 | evidence (screenshot path or file:line) | proposed micro-fix | files likely touched | boundary check: allowed / needs product decision (why)`
-Then: a **glance score** for your area (1–5: can a new PM get it in one look?) with one sentence of justification, and your **top 3 highest-impact fixes**.

Do not edit, create or delete any file and do not run any command that changes the repo, the app or the demo store (no Reset demo data, no clicks that save, decide, refresh or post). Do not run the gate script against port 3000. Observe and report only; your final message is your report.
-## Your area: Vehicle plan, requirement side panel and page, Replay, ripple
-Personas: Lena (`u-lena`), Wei (`u-wei`), Katrin (`u-katrin`).
-Question: **is the density right? What can collapse into a one-line summary?**

-Evidence: baseline screens `plan_*`, `requirement-panel_*`, `requirement-page_*`, `replay-score_*`, `replay-chain_*`, `ripple_*`, `ripple-drawer_*`. Code: `web/src/app/(app)/plan/*`, `web/src/components/requirements/*` (requirement-sheet, requirement-parts with Spec and TraceChain, provenance, quality-check, versions-panel, variants-compare, feedback-dialog), `web/src/app/(app)/requirements/[id]/requirement-view.tsx`, `web/src/components/replay/*`, `web/src/app/(app)/ripple/[id]/ripple-view.tsx`.

-Check: the provenance chips (they are honesty signals: keep visible, may be more compact), the quality-check strip, tabs and their counts, what is primary on the requirement, the replay header controls and beat panel, the ripple band/grid/drawer and its row actions.
-# UX intuitiveness pass: shared brief (goal, boundary, rubrics, app, output format)
-Every audit, fix and verification agent works from this brief. It is copied verbatim into each agent file in `.cursor/agents/`.
-## The goal

-The product must be **as easy to understand as Jira**: not the same features, the same level of "I get it at a glance". It should feel clean and calm, not overwhelming, while still giving enough context to be helpful. A product manager who has never seen it should know on each screen: **where am I, what needs my attention, what is the one next thing to do.**

-Background you can read (read-only): `web/README.md` (screens, personas, demo scripts), `docs/05-solution/ux-and-collaboration.md`, `docs/03-meetings/2026-10-10_2308_thomas-demo-feedback_summary.md` (BMW's feedback: "less is more", a PM must understand it "in one look").
-## THE BOUNDARY (read this twice)
-This pass changes **small details with a big UX impact**. It does **not** change the product.
-**Allowed (micro-level presentation):**

-- **Progressive disclosure:** a long analysis that is always shown becomes a one-line summary that expands into the full analysis on click. Secondary panels are collapsed by default. "Show more" on long lists.
-- **Visual hierarchy:** one clear primary button per screen or section; others become secondary/ghost. Mute metadata. Fix spacing, alignment and type scale. Reduce badge and colour noise.
-- **Microcopy:** button labels as verbs ("Confirm case", not "OK"), shorter headings, jargon explained with a tooltip or inline hint, consistent terms for the same thing across screens.
-- **States:** empty states that say what goes here and offer the one next action; loading skeletons; clear success/error toasts; disabled buttons say why they are disabled.
-- **Wayfinding:** breadcrumbs or back links, page titles that match the nav label, visible current location, sensible default sort and filter, counts on tabs.
-- **Accessibility:** focus states, keyboard reachability, contrast, labels, alt text, hit-target sizes.
-- Reusing existing shadcn components (Collapsible, Accordion, Tooltip, Skeleton, empty-state patterns) instead of custom ones.
-**Forbidden (if a finding needs one of these, report it under "Needs a product decision" and do NOT implement it):**
-- Adding, removing, merging or reordering screens, nav items, workflow steps, case/requirement states, outcomes or gates.
-- Changing roles, permissions, the data model, `web/src/contracts`, the mock backend logic (`web/src/mock`), the seed data or the AI behaviour.
-- Removing any information or feature. Hiding it behind a disclosure is fine, as long as it stays **reachable in one click** and the summary line tells you what's inside.

-- Hiding or weakening **honesty signals**: data-coverage warnings ("no China verbatims", "90% US"), evidence level, assumption vs. evidence labels, "no evidence" answers, quality-check issues, the AI-vs-human marking. These may be made more compact but must stay **visible without a click**. They are what the jury rewards.
-- Changing the demo storyline in `web/README.md` (the steps must still work exactly as written).
-- Visual redesign: new colour palette, new fonts, new layout system, restyled brand. Polish, don't redesign.
-When unsure: it's forbidden. Ask.
-## Rubrics

-- NN/g's 10 usability heuristics: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/ (cite by number 1–10: 1 visibility of system status, 2 match with the real world, 3 user control and freedom, 4 consistency and standards, 5 error prevention, 6 recognition rather than recall, 7 flexibility and efficiency, 8 aesthetic and minimalist design, 9 help users recognize/diagnose/recover from errors, 10 help and documentation).

-- Cognitive walkthrough, 4 questions per step: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/cognitive-walkthroughs/ (Will the user try to achieve the right result? Will they notice the correct action is available? Will they associate the action with the result? Will they see progress after the action?)
-- Progressive disclosure: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/progressive-disclosure/
-- Severity on Nielsen's 0–4 scale: 0 not a problem, 1 cosmetic, 2 minor, 3 major, 4 usability catastrophe.

-- Code rules: the Vercel Web Interface Guidelines in `.cursor/skills/web-design-guidelines/guidelines.md` (offline copy; source https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines/main/command.md).
-## The app

-- `web/` is Next.js 16, React 19, Tailwind 4, shadcn/ui (`web/src/components/ui`), a mock backend at `/api` (`web/src/mock`, do not change). Screens live in `web/src/app/(app)/*`, building blocks in `web/src/components/*`.

-- Nav (six items): My desk `/`, Inbox `/inbox`, Cases `/cases` (case page `/cases/<id>` with three steps: ① Evidence, ② Your stance `?step=knowledge`, ③ Requirements `?step=requirements`), Vehicle plan `/plan/G60`, Signals `/radar`, Innovation pool `/innovation`. Not in the nav: Settings `/settings`, Audit `/audit`, series brief `/brief` (persona menu), requirement page `/requirements/<id>`, ripple `/ripple/<id>`, Replay (overlay from the *Replay* button on a requirement).

-- Personas (cookie `rs_user`): `u-lena` (PM 5 Series RoW), `u-wei` (PM 5 Series China, not onboarded on a fresh store), `u-jonas` (HMI cross-series), `u-katrin` (head of product line), `u-sofia` (1 Series), `u-daniel` (7 Series).

-- **Baseline evidence (the "before")**: `docs/ux-audit/baseline/index.md` and `docs/ux-audit/baseline/screens/<state>_<1440|768>_<light|dark>.png`, plus axe and Lighthouse results in `docs/ux-audit/baseline/results.json`. Read the PNGs with the Read tool.

-- Extra headless screenshots of any state (no shared browser needed): `node .cursor/ux-gate/gate.mjs --out <dir> --only <names> --no-lighthouse` with targets from `.cursor/ux-gate/targets.json`. **Do not run it against port 3000 while other agents audit** (it resets the store); use `BASE_URL=http://localhost:3001` when a second server runs there.
-## Output format per finding
-One markdown table row each:

-`ID | screen/state | what's wrong (observed, not guessed) | heuristic # | severity 0–4 | evidence (screenshot path or file:line) | proposed micro-fix | files likely touched | boundary check: allowed / needs product decision (why)`
-Then: a **glance score** for your area (1–5: can a new PM get it in one look?) with one sentence of justification, and your **top 3 highest-impact fixes**.

+- Code rules: the Vercel Web Interface Guidelines in `.cursor/skills/web-design-guidelines/guidelines.md` (offline copy; source https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines/main/command.md).
+## The app

+- `web/` is Next.js 16, React 19, Tailwind 4, shadcn/ui (`web/src/components/ui`), a mock backend at `/api` (`web/src/mock`, do not change). Screens live in `web/src/app/(app)/*`, building blocks in `web/src/components/*`.

+- Nav (six items): My desk `/`, Inbox `/inbox`, Cases `/cases` (case page `/cases/<id>` with three steps: ① Evidence, ② Your stance `?step=knowledge`, ③ Requirements `?step=requirements`), Vehicle plan `/plan/G60`, Signals `/radar`, Innovation pool `/innovation`. Not in the nav: Settings `/settings`, Audit `/audit`, series brief `/brief` (persona menu), requirement page `/requirements/<id>`, ripple `/ripple/<id>`, Replay (overlay from the *Replay* button on a requirement).

+- Personas (cookie `rs_user`): `u-lena` (PM 5 Series RoW), `u-wei` (PM 5 Series China, not onboarded on a fresh store), `u-jonas` (HMI cross-series), `u-katrin` (head of product line), `u-sofia` (1 Series), `u-daniel` (7 Series).

+- **Baseline evidence (the "before")**: `docs/ux-audit/baseline/index.md` and `docs/ux-audit/baseline/screens/<state>_<1440|768>_<light|dark>.png`, plus axe and Lighthouse results in `docs/ux-audit/baseline/results.json`. Read the PNGs with the Read tool.

+- Extra headless screenshots of any state (no shared browser needed): `node .cursor/ux-gate/gate.mjs --out <dir> --only <names> --no-lighthouse` with targets from `.cursor/ux-gate/targets.json`. **Do not run it against port 3000 while other agents audit** (it resets the store); use `BASE_URL=http://localhost:3001` when a second server runs there.
+## Output format per finding
+One markdown table row each:

+`ID | screen/state | what's wrong (observed, not guessed) | heuristic # | severity 0–4 | evidence (screenshot path or file:line) | proposed micro-fix | files likely touched | boundary check: allowed / needs product decision (why)`
+Then: a **glance score** for your area (1–5: can a new PM get it in one look?) with one sentence of justification, and your **top 3 highest-impact fixes**.

> # UX and Collaboration Design (demo v1)
> 
> The decisions behind the clickable demo in [`web/`](../../web/README.md). Agreed with Amine on 10.10.2026; the code follows this page. Related: [end-to-end-flow.md](end-to-end-flow.md), [web-intelligence-loop.md](web-i
> 
> **Where this page goes beyond the backend (checked 2026-10-11).** This page describes the UI demo, which runs on a mock contract. The backend in `backend/` currently has less:
> - **Case states:** the backend has observed → open → confirmed / rejected (plus merge and split). Investigating, awaiting answers, ready to decide, referred, innovation pool and parked exist only in the UI.
> - **Requirement states:** the backend has draft → in discussion → approved / rejected, and delete as a tombstone. Head sign-off, planned and exported exist only in the UI.
> - **Roles:** the backend knows PM and engineer actors. Attribute PMs, the head of product line, referrals and escalations exist only in the UI.
> - **Facets:** the backend stores car area, topic, aspect group, scope, brand fit, segment and release fit. "Type" and "change depth" exist only in the UI; "scope global / RoW / China" is a config per vehicle and market
> - **Not in the backend:** vehicle plan and planned features, meeting prep and answers from pasted notes, the monitor's alerts (the backend only flags new evidence), export.
> 
> ## 1. Who works in the tool
> 
> Research on how OEM product management is organized (sources in the session notes):
> - At BMW, product roles sit in two lines. **Sales/brand product management** includes market PMs, who define market requirements per series. **Development product lines** have an overall project lead per derivative.

1	# BMW Challenge: AI for Product Decision Making
2	
3	An AI-powered application that helps BMW product managers derive, justify and prioritize customer requirements for a successor vehicle, with the product manager in control of every decision. This folder holds the challenge material, provided data, meeting notes and team ideas.
4	
5	## Structure
6	
7	```
8	docs/
9	├── GLOSSARY.md                Model codes, BMW and process terms, German option-list terms
10	├── 01-challenge/              What we are asked to build, and what BMW wants
11	├── 02-bmw-data/    Provided BMW data: raw/, processed/ (CSV and text), insights, equipment baseline
12	├── 03-meetings/       Meeting summaries and notes (raw/ holds the transcripts)
13	├── 04-team-notes/             Our early brainstorm, open questions, notes between teammates
14	├── 05-web-sources/            External sources for the fetch agents
15	└── 06-solution-concept/       Solution concept from the UI side: scope, end-to-end flow, UX decisions
16	```
17	
18	This is the single knowledge base: the former `docs/` folder of the frontend branch was merged into it on 2026-10-11 (identical files dropped, new files moved here). The fixed classification lives in [`../taxonomy/`](../taxonomy/README.md).
19	
20	The decided design is not in this folder: see [`../architecture.mmd`](../architecture.mmd) and [`../data-model.mmd`](../data-model.mmd).
21	
22	### 01-challenge: the task
23	| File | Content |
24	|---|---|
25	| [`hackathon-briefing.md`](01-challenge/hackathon-briefing.md) / [`.pdf`](01-challenge/hackathon-briefing.pdf) | The challenge, why it matters, mission, what to demonstrate |
26	| [`mission-and-deliverables.md`](01-challenge/mission-and-deliverables.md) | Mission sheet: scope, in/out of scope, expected deliverables, audit trail |
27	| [`process-cycle.md`](01-challenge/process-cycle.md) | BMW's process slide: situation analysis → documentation (also drawn in [`../layers.mmd`](../layers.mmd)) |
28	| [`findings-to-requirements.md`](01-challenge/findings-to-requirements.md) | 1 billion findings → 1,000 requirements → one car |
29	| [`provided-data-overview.md`](01-challenge/provided-data-overview.md) | What each provided dataset is good for |
30	| [`evaluation-criteria.md`](01-challenge/evaluation-criteria.md) | The 5 judging criteria, "we reward honesty", what to show for each |
31	| [`stakeholder-needs.md`](01-challenge/stakeholder-needs.md) | Consolidated needs from all documents and interviews, with source tags |
32	| [`smart-requirements.md`](01-challenge/smart-requirements.md) | How to write a requirement (SMART), good and bad examples, the requirement record template |
33	| [`product-development-process.md`](01-challenge/product-development-process.md) | Generic 13-phase automotive process with gates, and where our tool sits |
34	| `assets/` | The source slide images |
35	
36	### 02-bmw-data: the data
37	Start with [`02-bmw-data/README.md`](02-bmw-data/README.md) (columns, counts, caveats). Files in `raw/`: customer feedback (F70, G60, G70), customer study 2025, sales volumes 2024 to 2030, and option lists (PDF). Never modify `raw/`.
38	
39	| File | Content |
40	|---|---|
41	| [`insights.md`](02-bmw-data/insights.md) | Pre-computed findings: coverage, cross-model themes, per-model tables, conflicting signals |
42	| [`equipment-baseline.md`](02-bmw-data/equipment-baseline.md) | English summary of the option lists: line-ups, prices, standard and optional equipment |
43	| [`external-sources.md`](02-bmw-data/external-sources.md) | Competitors named, suggested benchmarks, evidence trust levels (the source list itself is in `05-web-sources/`) |
44	| `processed/` | Derived, agent-readable files built from `raw/`: `feedback_rows.csv` (13,771 rows, one per verbatim x topic; read by `taxonomy/build.py`), `feedback_verbatims.csv` (10,128), `feedback_topic_counts.csv`, `study_cn_eu_2025.csv`, `study_us_2025.csv`, `sales_volumes.csv`, `option-lists/*.txt` |
45	| [`scripts/build_processed.py`](02-bmw-data/scripts/build_processed.py) | Rebuilds `processed/` from `raw/` |
46	
47	### 03-meetings: what was said
48	Files are named `date_time_topic_type`. Read the summaries and notes first; raw transcripts are in `raw/`.
49	
50	| Meeting | Transcript | Summary / notes |
51	|---|---|---|
52	| Team discussion, 14:24 (German) | [transcript](03-meetings/raw/2026-10-10_1424_team-discussion-de_transcript.md) | [summary](03-meetings/2026-10-10_1424_team-discussion-de_summary.md) |
53	| Team discussion with BMW contact, 14:39 (English) | [transcript](03-meetings/raw/2026-10-10_1439_team-discussion-en_transcript.md) | [summary](03-meetings/2026-10-10_1439_team-discussion-en_summary.md) |
54	| Product manager interview 1 (about 24 min) | [transcript](03-meetings/raw/2026-10-10_pm-interview_transcript.md) | [summary](03-meetings/2026-10-10_pm-interview_summary.md) |
55	| Product manager interview 2, 16:05 to 16:46 | not stored | [notes](03-meetings/2026-10-10_1605_pm-interview-2_notes.md) |
56	| Demo feedback from Thomas (BMW AI engineer), 23:08 (about 26 min): fixed taxonomy, one kanban for cases, less is more | [transcript](03-meetings/raw/2026-10-10_2308_thomas-demo-feedback_transcript.md) | [summary](03-meetings/2026-10-10_2308_thomas-demo-feedback_summary.md) |
57	| Lifecycle voice note, 18:04 (about 1.5 min) | [transcript](03-meetings/raw/2026-10-10_1804_lifecycle-voice-note_transcript.md) | [summary](03-meetings/2026-10-10_1804_lifecycle-voice-note_summary.md) |
58	
59	The two PM interviews are the most important user input.
60	
61	### 04-team-notes: our early thinking
62	[`brainstorm-ideas.md`](04-team-notes/brainstorm-ideas.md): data sources, markets, architecture layers, agents, perspectives. Superseded by the architecture files where they differ.
63	[`open-design-questions.md`](04-team-notes/open-design-questions.md): two open prompts on the PM workflow and UX.
64	[`notes-to-ghassen/2026-10-11_taxonomy-categories.md`](04-team-notes/notes-to-ghassen/2026-10-11_taxonomy-categories.md): the note that introduced the fixed taxonomy (it says "finding"; that is our "signal").
65	
66	### 05-web-sources: external data
67	[`fetching-sources.md`](05-web-sources/fetching-sources.md): what to search for, the list of web sources with URLs (including sources for new launches and competitor generations), coverage per model and market, the fetch order, and what to save with every record.
68	
69	### 06-solution-concept: the concept from the UI side
70	[`scope-and-focus.md`](06-solution-concept/scope-and-focus.md), [`end-to-end-flow.md`](06-solution-concept/end-to-end-flow.md), [`ux-and-collaboration.md`](06-solution-concept/ux-and-collaboration.md), [`web-intelligence-loop.md`](06-solution-concept/web-intelligence-loop.md). Written on the frontend branch; where they differ from `CLAUDE.md`, `architecture.mmd` or `database-design.md`, those win for the backend.
71	
72	## Recurring themes across the material
73	- **Human in the loop, no black box:** every recommendation shows its source, market and evidence. The product manager accepts, edits or rejects.
74	- **Traceability and audit trail:** from signal, to case, to requirement, to score, to decision, including who changed what, when and why.
75	- **Evidence vs. assumption:** make clear which conclusions rest on data and which on forward-looking assumptions.
76	- **Continuous loop:** competitor and feedback agents re-check requirements and flag outdated ones. They do not overwrite.
77	- **Brand fit and market differences:** volume of mentions is not relevance. China, the US and the Middle East need separate treatment.
78	- **Prioritization signals:** count distinct customers, not reach or rows. Treat functional complaints and removed features as serious.
79	- **Interview 2 additions:** the PM sets priorities (weight profiles) and wants to see how the ranking changes; skip sources; surface market conflicts instead of deciding them.
80	- **Lifecycle:** a new generation can change everything, a mid-life update only small things (colours, rims); too big for an update means next generation, not "no".
