# BMW Challenge: AI for Product Decision Making

An AI-powered application that helps BMW product managers derive, justify and prioritize customer requirements for a successor vehicle, with the product manager in control of every decision. This folder holds the challenge material, provided data, meeting notes and team ideas.

## Structure

```
docs/
├── GLOSSARY.md                Model codes, BMW and process terms, German option-list terms
├── 01-challenge/              What we are asked to build, and what BMW wants
├── 02-bmw-data/    Provided BMW data: raw/, processed/ (CSV and text), insights, equipment baseline
├── 03-meetings/       Meeting summaries and notes (raw/ holds the transcripts)
├── 04-team-notes/             Our early brainstorm, open questions, notes between teammates
├── 05-web-sources/            External sources for the fetch agents
└── 06-solution-concept/       Solution concept from the UI side: scope, end-to-end flow, UX decisions
```

This is the single knowledge base: the former `docs/` folder of the frontend branch was merged into it on 2026-10-11 (identical files dropped, new files moved here). The fixed classification lives in [`../taxonomy/`](../taxonomy/README.md).

The decided design is not in this folder: see [`../architecture.mmd`](../architecture.mmd) and [`../data-model.mmd`](../data-model.mmd).

### 01-challenge: the task
| File | Content |
|---|---|
| [`hackathon-briefing.md`](01-challenge/hackathon-briefing.md) / [`.pdf`](01-challenge/hackathon-briefing.pdf) | The challenge, why it matters, mission, what to demonstrate |
| [`mission-and-deliverables.md`](01-challenge/mission-and-deliverables.md) | Mission sheet: scope, in/out of scope, expected deliverables, audit trail |
| [`process-cycle.md`](01-challenge/process-cycle.md) | BMW's process slide: situation analysis → documentation (also drawn in [`../layers.mmd`](../layers.mmd)) |
| [`findings-to-requirements.md`](01-challenge/findings-to-requirements.md) | 1 billion findings → 1,000 requirements → one car |
| [`provided-data-overview.md`](01-challenge/provided-data-overview.md) | What each provided dataset is good for |
| [`evaluation-criteria.md`](01-challenge/evaluation-criteria.md) | The 5 judging criteria, "we reward honesty", what to show for each |
| [`stakeholder-needs.md`](01-challenge/stakeholder-needs.md) | Consolidated needs from all documents and interviews, with source tags |
| [`smart-requirements.md`](01-challenge/smart-requirements.md) | How to write a requirement (SMART), good and bad examples, the requirement record template |
| [`product-development-process.md`](01-challenge/product-development-process.md) | Generic 13-phase automotive process with gates, and where our tool sits |
| `assets/` | The source slide images |

### 02-bmw-data: the data
Start with [`02-bmw-data/README.md`](02-bmw-data/README.md) (columns, counts, caveats). Files in `raw/`: customer feedback (F70, G60, G70), customer study 2025, sales volumes 2024 to 2030, and option lists (PDF). Never modify `raw/`.

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| [`insights.md`](02-bmw-data/insights.md) | Pre-computed findings: coverage, cross-model themes, per-model tables, conflicting signals |
| [`equipment-baseline.md`](02-bmw-data/equipment-baseline.md) | English summary of the option lists: line-ups, prices, standard and optional equipment |
| [`external-sources.md`](02-bmw-data/external-sources.md) | Competitors named, suggested benchmarks, evidence trust levels (the source list itself is in `05-web-sources/`) |
| `processed/` | Derived, agent-readable files built from `raw/`: `feedback_rows.csv` (13,771 rows, one per verbatim x topic; read by `taxonomy/build.py`), `feedback_verbatims.csv` (10,128), `feedback_topic_counts.csv`, `study_cn_eu_2025.csv`, `study_us_2025.csv`, `sales_volumes.csv`, `option-lists/*.txt` |
| [`scripts/build_processed.py`](02-bmw-data/scripts/build_processed.py) | Rebuilds `processed/` from `raw/` |

### 03-meetings: what was said
Files are named `date_time_topic_type`. Read the summaries and notes first; raw transcripts are in `raw/`.

| Meeting | Transcript | Summary / notes |
|---|---|---|
| Team discussion, 14:24 (German) | [transcript](03-meetings/raw/2026-10-10_1424_team-discussion-de_transcript.md) | [summary](03-meetings/2026-10-10_1424_team-discussion-de_summary.md) |
| Team discussion with BMW contact, 14:39 (English) | [transcript](03-meetings/raw/2026-10-10_1439_team-discussion-en_transcript.md) | [summary](03-meetings/2026-10-10_1439_team-discussion-en_summary.md) |
| Product manager interview 1 (about 24 min) | [transcript](03-meetings/raw/2026-10-10_pm-interview_transcript.md) | [summary](03-meetings/2026-10-10_pm-interview_summary.md) |
| Product manager interview 2, 16:05 to 16:46 | not stored | [notes](03-meetings/2026-10-10_1605_pm-interview-2_notes.md) |
| Demo feedback from Thomas (BMW AI engineer), 23:08 (about 26 min): fixed taxonomy, one kanban for cases, less is more | [transcript](03-meetings/raw/2026-10-10_2308_thomas-demo-feedback_transcript.md) | [summary](03-meetings/2026-10-10_2308_thomas-demo-feedback_summary.md) |
| Lifecycle voice note, 18:04 (about 1.5 min) | [transcript](03-meetings/raw/2026-10-10_1804_lifecycle-voice-note_transcript.md) | [summary](03-meetings/2026-10-10_1804_lifecycle-voice-note_summary.md) |

The two PM interviews are the most important user input.

### 04-team-notes: our early thinking
[`brainstorm-ideas.md`](04-team-notes/brainstorm-ideas.md): data sources, markets, architecture layers, agents, perspectives. Superseded by the architecture files where they differ.
[`open-design-questions.md`](04-team-notes/open-design-questions.md): two open prompts on the PM workflow and UX.
[`notes-to-ghassen/2026-10-11_taxonomy-categories.md`](04-team-notes/notes-to-ghassen/2026-10-11_taxonomy-categories.md): the note that introduced the fixed taxonomy (it says "finding"; that is our "signal").

### 05-web-sources: external data
[`fetching-sources.md`](05-web-sources/fetching-sources.md): what to search for, the list of web sources with URLs (including sources for new launches and competitor generations), coverage per model and market, the fetch order, and what to save with every record.

### 06-solution-concept: the concept from the UI side
[`scope-and-focus.md`](06-solution-concept/scope-and-focus.md), [`end-to-end-flow.md`](06-solution-concept/end-to-end-flow.md), [`ux-and-collaboration.md`](06-solution-concept/ux-and-collaboration.md), [`web-intelligence-loop.md`](06-solution-concept/web-intelligence-loop.md). Written on the frontend branch; where they differ from `CLAUDE.md`, `architecture.mmd` or `database-design.md`, those win for the backend.

## Recurring themes across the material
- **Human in the loop, no black box:** every recommendation shows its source, market and evidence. The product manager accepts, edits or rejects.
- **Traceability and audit trail:** from signal, to case, to requirement, to score, to decision, including who changed what, when and why.
- **Evidence vs. assumption:** make clear which conclusions rest on data and which on forward-looking assumptions.
- **Continuous loop:** competitor and feedback agents re-check requirements and flag outdated ones. They do not overwrite.
- **Brand fit and market differences:** volume of mentions is not relevance. China, the US and the Middle East need separate treatment.
- **Prioritization signals:** count distinct customers, not reach or rows. Treat functional complaints and removed features as serious.
- **Interview 2 additions:** the PM sets priorities (weight profiles) and wants to see how the ranking changes; skip sources; surface market conflicts instead of deciding them.
- **Lifecycle:** a new generation can change everything, a mid-life update only small things (colours, rims); too big for an update means next generation, not "no".
- **Output is a shortlist:** PMs hand roughly the top 10 requirements to engineering (codebeamer), each with its arguments.
- **Scope:** customer value only. No regulatory, engineering or business-case work.

AI that turns customer voice, market data and competitor research into prioritized, evidence-backed requirements for the next BMW, with the product manager in control of every decision.

TUM.ai Hackathon Final · BMW Group challenge "AI for Product Decision Making"

--- ## The problem A BMW product manager defining the **successor** of a vehicle line (3 to 5 years ahead) has to read thousands of customer verbatims, customer studies, option lists, competitor news and trend reports, then argue for the roughly **top 10 requirements** that go to engineering. In interviews, BMW PMs told us research is the bottleneck, and that a tool is only useful if it is **no black box**: every proposal must show its source, market and evidence, and the PM decides. ## What Argon does ``` Signal ──► Case (problem) ──► PM confirms ──► Requirement (solution) ──► PM approves ──► engineering ``` | Step | What it is | Who acts | |---|---|---| | **Signal** | One statement about one feature from one source record (a BMW verbatim, a review sentence, a competitor fact, a trend), with the exact quote, market and source link. Invalid signals go to a visible quarantine. | AI extracts, a validation gate checks every quote against the stored record | | **Case** | A customer problem built from a group of signals, e.g. *"Front seat ventilation too weak"*. Keeps all opinions per market and powertrain, so market conflicts become visible. Scored, but has no cost. | AI clusters, figures and tags; **PM confirms or rejects** | | **Requirement** | What BMW will build, customer-facing and measurable: target vs. today's value and competitors, acceptance criteria, release (next generation, mid-life update, OTA), rough cost S/M/L. Every sentence carries its provenance: evidence, PM context or assumption. | AI drafts after confirmation; **PM approves**, head of product line signs off | Everything is written to an **append-only audit trail** (actor, timestamp, before/after, rationale), from the source record to the human decision. A *trace replay* plays a requirement's whole life in about 15 seconds and re-checks the chain: every quote found in its source, every record hash intact, no gaps, a rationale on every status change. ### Highlights - **Fixed taxonomy, no invented themes.** Every signal is classified into BMW's own labels: 219 topics, 11 aspect groups, 11 car areas ([`taxonomy/`](taxonomy/README.md)). - **Explainable, tunable score.** Case score = weighted factors (distinct customers, severity, satisfaction gap, competitor gap, market volume, removed vs. predecessor, capped reach, trend) × brand-fit multiplier. The PM switches weight profiles and sees which items stay on top regardless. Requirement rank = case score × cost multiplier. - **Reach is not relevance.** Distinct customers and capped reach keep one influencer from outranking a hundred owners. - **Markets are separate worlds.** Conflicts (one market negative, another positive) are flagged with statistics and never decided by the AI. - **Argus, the AI assistant.** A RAG sidebar on every case and requirement page that cites a signal ID for every claim ("no evidence found" otherwise) and proposes edits as diffs the PM accepts or rejects. - **Daily web loop.** Competitor, customer, trend and innovation agents fetch from a curated source list within a daily budget; page content is treated as data, and agents can only write signals, never cases. - **Collaboration built in.** Case ownership per line, series briefs, stances, open questions, referrals, an innovation pool, the vehicle plan and Codebeamer-style export. ## Run it **Demo UI (offline, synthetic data on top of real BMW verbatims):** ```bash cd web && npm install && npm run dev ``` Open http://localhost:3000, pick a persona, and use **Reset demo data** in the persona menu. Demo scripts are in [`web/README.md`](web/README.md). **Backend on a local embedded database (no Supabase, no OpenAI):** ```bash cd backend && uv run python -m app.dev_local ``` Then start the UI against it with `DATA_SOURCE=backend` (API on `http://localhost:8000`, OpenAPI at `/docs`). Tests run offline with `uv run pytest`. For the full Supabase + OpenAI setup, copy `backend/.env.example` to `backend/.env` and see [`backend/API.md`](backend/API.md) and [`HANDOFF.md`](HANDOFF.md). ## Architecture | Layer | Tech | |---|---| | UI | Next.js 16, React, Tailwind, shadcn/ui, TanStack Query; typed REST contract in Zod ([`web/src/contracts`](web/src/contracts), exported to [`contracts/`](contracts/openapi.yaml)) | | API and agents | Python 3.12, FastAPI, background fetch worker | | Storage | Supabase Postgres + pgvector (16 migrations), append-only audit table enforced in the database | | AI | OpenAI chat models for classification, extraction, case pages, tags, Argus and requirement texts; `text-embedding-3-small` (768 dims) for clustering and hybrid search. Every output stores its model and prompt version | Pipeline: configuration → one-time seed of BMW's data → daily fetch loop → signal validation gate → cases → case score → PM workspace → requirement generation → ranking and approval. The full diagram is [`architecture.mmd`](architecture.mmd). ## Data BMW provided customer feedback for the 1, 5 and 7 Series (about 10,000 verbatims), a 2025 customer study, sales volumes to 2030 and German option lists. They are kept unmodified in [`docs/02-bmw-data/raw/`](docs/02-bmw-data/README.md) and loaded from the original files, so every value keeps its sheet and row. Competitors and 3-to-5-year trends come only from web research and are labelled as external or assumption. Known gaps (no Chinese feedback, US-heavy 5 and 7 Series data, no dates, no study sample sizes) are shown in the product, not hidden. ## Repository | Path | Content | |---|---| | [`web/`](web/README.md) | The Argon UI and an offline mock backend that serves the same contract | | [`backend/`](backend/API.md) | API, agents, scoring, seed, Supabase migrations, tests and reports | | [`taxonomy/`](taxonomy/README.md) | The fixed classification (car areas, topics, aspect groups), build script and classifier eval | | [`contracts/`](contracts/openapi.yaml) | REST contract between UI and backend (OpenAPI 3.1 + JSON Schemas) | | [`docs/`](docs/README.md) | Challenge brief, provided data, PM interviews and meeting notes, web source list | | [`docs/`](docs/) | UI solution design, design assets and logos, UX audit reports | | [`landing/`](landing/index.html) | Intro loading page | | [`architecture.mmd`](architecture.mmd), [`database-design.md`](database-design.md), [`data-model.mmd`](data-model.mmd) | Pipeline, database design and ER diagram | | [`plan.md`](plan.md), [`changes.md`](changes.md), [`HANDOFF.md`](HANDOFF.md) | Implementation plan, every changed decision with its reason, current state | ## Team Built in one weekend at the TUM.ai hackathon by [Ghassen Zaara](https://github.com/ghassenzaara), [kechich](https://github.com/kechich), [Ahlem Trabelsi](https://github.com/ahlemtr) and [Amine Cheikhrouhou](https://github.com/AmineChr54). AI-assisted development sessions are recorded with [Entire](https://entire.io). A hackathon prototype, not an official BMW product. BMW data was provided for the challenge.

content.text:
Both commits are on `main` and the new README shows correctly on GitHub, logo included. The About section and tags are not done: they need admin rights on the repo, and your account only has write access.

**README** ([README.md](README.md))
- The Argon logo and name at the top, with a light and a dark version so it shows on both GitHub themes.
- Sections: the problem, how Signal → Case → Requirement works and who acts at each step, highlights, how to run it, the tech stack, the data and its known gaps, a map of the repo, and the team with GitHub links.

**One `docs/` folder** (replaces `All-context/` and the old `docs/`)
- `docs/` now holds `01-challenge`, `02-bmw-data`, `03-meetings`, `04-team-notes`, `05-web-sources`, `06-solution-concept`, plus `design/`, `ux-audit/`, `assets/` and `archive/`. [docs/README.md](docs/README.md) indexes all of it.
- The old copy of the challenge files, data and meeting notes was deleted with your OK. Its meeting notes still named BMW staff, which the newer copy had removed.
- The two solution-concept versions had both changed, so neither could just go. kechich's newer version is now the main one. Ahlem's earlier version is kept in `docs/archive/` so nothing is lost.
- Everything that pointed to the old folders now points to the new paths: the backend data paths, the web source list, the taxonomy build, the web seed script, `CLAUDE.md` and the docs. The BMW raw files moved unchanged. Moving them doesn't affect what's already loaded in Supabase, because it refers to files by storage keys, not repo paths.
- A link check over all Markdown files found no new broken links. Per the repo rules I didn't run the backend tests or the web build, so the code changes are only checked by reading them.
- I also deleted a personal `.vscode/settings.json` and added a note on the move to `changes.md`.

**Entire**
Your team's checkpoint data is already on GitHub: 35 checkpoints, linked from 34 commits on `main`. That's what Verify reads, and it looks fine. Entire is not switched on for your own machine, so this session wasn't recorded, which doesn't block the check. Paste the repo link on the submission page and press **Verify** now; if it shows ✗, send me the message.

gh repo edit ghassenzaara/BMW-Product-Management-Challenge --description "Argon: AI platform that turns BMW customer feedback, studies and competitor research into prioritized, evidence-backed vehicle requirements, with the product manager in control and a full audit trail. ```
He can also paste the same text in the gear icon next to "About" on the repo page.

The repo is public and includes BMW's raw data files and the agents' session transcripts. That was already the case before my changes, and deleting files doesn't remove them from git history. If the challenge terms don't allow publishing that data, you'll need to deal with it separately.

    pass


OPEN_MIN_CUSTOMERS = 20   # distinct BMW customers of one line
OPEN_MIN_DEFECTS = 10     # distinct BMW customers of one line who report a defect


def open_reason(vehicle_figures: dict, thresholds: dict) -> str | None:
    """The rule that opens a case for a line, or None. A handful of comments is no
    reason to change a car: a case needs enough distinct customers who complain or
    wish for something (praise alone is a strength to protect, not a problem), or
    enough customers reporting a defect, a competitor gap or a removed feature."""
    markets = vehicle_figures.get("markets", {})
    customers = vehicle_figures.get("distinct_customers", 0)
    negative = sum(m["complaints"] + m["wishes"] for m in markets.values())
    likes = sum(m["likes"] for m in markets.values())
